do_not_lead_with: Do not lead with the 47.3% alternatives allocation, the Asia real estate concentration, or the over-limit position. These are the pressure points from the last three conversations, and re-opening on them would amount to pressing Mr. Tan again on the very issue he's asked for time on — even framed as "concern," it will read as renewed pressure. Also avoid leading with the mandate/plan mismatch as a compliance-style correction; that's a findings-review posture, not a relationship one, and this is the fourth time around this topic.
one_number: 47.3% (the alternatives allocation) — have it ready to cite precisely if he asks "where do things stand," but do not volunteer it as the opener.
open_with: Open on the relationship, not the portfolio: acknowledge that this is now the fourth time you're both sitting down on this same topic, thank him for his patience and candor, and explicitly honor that he asked for more time — make clear you're not here to press him again today. Let him set the pace of the conversation from there. Only after that acknowledgment, gently note that given his age and health, you'd feel more comfortable if there were at least a simple check-in cadence or a named point of contact (family member, executor, whoever he trusts) so that nothing sits unattended — framed as care and continuity, not as sales pressure. This gives you a legitimate, low-pressure way to touch the "open loop nobody is tracking" without reopening the allocation debate he's asked to pause.
